title: ActQuant: Sub-4-bit Action-Guided Backbone Weight-Only Quantization for Vision-Language-Action Models
claim: Ours keeps accuracy at extreme compression where baselines collapse, and uniquely covers more capabilities while shrinking memory severalfold.
layout: 3 panels: left line plot, right-top feature table, right-bottom bar chart
description: A three-panel composite. Panel (a) on the left is a line plot of LIBERO success rate versus Vision+LLM bits-per-weight from 2.0 to 4.0. A dotted line marks the fp16 ceiling at 97%. The purple ActQuant curve stays high, while AWQ, GPTQ and QVLA drop steeply at low bit-width. A broken axis shows the baselines collapsing to 0 at 2.0 bpw, flagged by a red 'baselines collapse' arrow. Panel (b), top right, is a checkmark/cross table. It compares QAIL, BitVLA, QVLA, QuantVLA and ActQuant (highlighted in grey) across mixed precision, fine-tuning-free, real-world experiments, extreme quantization and the quantized components. Panel (c), bottom right, is a horizontal bar chart of memory. The dark fp16 bar is 14.3 GB, and shorter gold ActQuant bars at 4.0 to 2.5 bpw carry labels for compression ratio and success rate.
caption: (a) Average success rate on LIBERO ($\pi_{0.5}$) as the backbone bit-width drops from $4.0$ to $2.0$ bpw. (b) Comparison of ActQuant with other VLA quantization methods. (c) Backbone memory usage across average bit-widths, with compression ratio against the baseline and success rate (SR).
abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models exhibit remarkable action generation for embodied intelligence, but their heavy compute make deployment on edge platforms impractical. Aggressive, sub-4-bit weight quantization is the natural solution, yet existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods suffer severe performance degradation in this regime. To address this, we introduce ActQuant, an action-guided mixed-precision PTQ framework that operates in two stages: (1) an inter-tensor bit allocator that assigns each weight matrix a single bit-width based on how much it contributes to predicting the agent's actions; (2) an intra-tensor scale optimizer tunes per-block quantization scales using action-aware curvature, so that dynamic range is concentrated on the weights most influential for control. To deliver the on-device benefits of our aggressive quantization, we further introduce OmniModel.cpp, an agentic conversion pipeline that ports architectures into a native C/C++ runtime with efficient low-bit kernels. We evaluate ActQuant both in simulation and on a real-world 6-DoF UR3 arm, with all models deployed through OmniModel.cpp. On the LIBERO benchmark, ActQuant is the only method that operates at or below 3 bits-per-weight, retaining 95.0% on OpenVLA-OFT and 94.8% on $Ï_{0.5}$. Pushed further, ActQuant reaches 2.5 bpw at 90.1% on OpenVLA-OFT, compressing the backbone from 14.3 GB to 2.7 GB (5.3$\times$). On the physical UR3 arm, $Ï_{0.5}$ quantized with ActQuant retains the baseline's success rate while reducing the memory footprint by 2.5$\times$.
